passages.t: ‘O LORD, You have searched me and known me’, and ‘Where can I flee?’
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David” (verse 1). Then: “O LORD, You have searched me and known me” (verse 1).

God knows everything about the singer. “You know when I sit and when I rise; You understand my thoughts from afar” (verse 2). He knows the path and the resting (verse 3). “Even before a word is on my tongue, You know all about it, O LORD” (verse 4). “You hem me in behind and before; You have laid Your hand upon me” (verse 5). “Such knowledge is too wonderful for me” (verse 6).

And God is everywhere. “Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?” (verse 7). “If I ascend to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there” (verse 8). Even at the far east where the dawn rises, or the farthest sea, “even there Your hand will guide me; Your right hand will hold me fast” (verses 9 and 10). Even the dark cannot hide him, “for darkness is as light to You” (verse 12).
passages.hearers:
Many Bible readers love this psalm. It is a prayer, not a lecture. The singer does not say ‘God knows everything’. He says ‘You know me’.

‘Hem me in’ (verse 5) could feel like a trap. But the next line is gentle: a hand laid on someone's shoulder. Being fully known by God is frightening and comforting at once.

The places in verses 8 and 9 cover the whole world as an Israelite pictured it: up to the heavens, down to Sheol, east to the dawn, west to the far sea, the Mediterranean. Sheol was the place of the dead. Other psalms ask whether God is praised there (Psalm 6:5), as the book page's part on Sheol explains. Psalm 139 says something bold: even there, God is present.

Jonah tried to run “away from the presence of the LORD” (Jonah 1:3), and found out what verse 7 means.
passages.later:
God asked through Jeremiah, “Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” (Jeremiah 23:24). Hebrews says, “Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight” (Hebrews 4:13).

Paul told the people of Athens that God “is not far from each one of us” (Acts 17:27). And he was sure that nothing, “neither height nor depth”, can separate believers from God's love (Romans 8:39).
passages.asks:
Do you find it frightening or comforting that God knows you completely? Psalm 139 holds both. He knows the worst about you, and he has not let go.

If you have tried to run from God, or felt you were too far gone, read verses 7 to 12 slowly. There is no place, not even the darkest one, where his hand cannot reach you.

passages.t: ‘You knit me together in my mother’s womb’
passages.happening:
Now the singer looks back to before he was born. “For You formed my inmost being; You knit me together in my mother's womb” (verse 13). “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Marvelous are Your works, and I know this very well” (verse 14).

“My frame was not hidden from You when I was made in secret, when I was woven together in the depths of the earth” (verse 15). “Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in Your book and ordained for me before one of them came to be” (verse 16).

He is amazed. “How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God, how vast is their sum!” (verse 17). They outnumber the grains of sand, “and when I awake, I am still with You” (verse 18).
passages.hearers:
The pictures come from the crafts of weaving and needlework. God ‘knit’ him, and he was ‘woven together’, like a fine piece of cloth made with care. ‘The depths of the earth’ (verse 15) is probably a poetic picture of the hidden, dark place of the womb. Job uses the same picture: “You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews” (Job 10:11).

‘Fearfully and wonderfully made’ means made in a way that fills you with awe. The singer is not boasting about himself. He is praising the One who made him.

Notice what the passage says. God knew this person, and was at work making him, before he was born. His eyes saw him when he was still unformed. His life was in God's care before a single day of it was lived.

This is true of every person. Every person, with any disability or illness, is made by God and is precious to him. No one is a mistake. When Jesus' disciples asked whose sin had caused a man to be born blind, he answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned” (John 9:3).
passages.later: God said to Jeremiah, “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you” (Jeremiah 1:5). Paul wrote, “For we are God's workmanship” (Ephesians 2:10). Jesus said, “even the very hairs of your head are all numbered” (Matthew 10:30).
passages.hard:
These verses are often quoted in debates about abortion. Here is what the text says. It says that God knows and cares for a person before birth, that he is at work forming that person in the womb, and that the person's life is in his hands from the start. Christians apply this to hard questions about law and medicine with care, and they do not all draw every conclusion in the same way. These notes take no political position and speak for no party or law.

If you carry grief or guilt about a pregnancy, or about the loss of a child before or after birth, please know that you are met with gentleness here, not judgment. God knows your story too. Please talk with a trusted pastor or friend. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.
passages.asks:
Do you believe you were made with care? Many people grow up hearing they were an accident, or a disappointment, or not enough. Psalm 139 says that God made you on purpose, and that he knew you before anyone else did.

And it asks how you look at others. If every person was knit together by God, then no one is worthless: not the person with a disability, not the unborn, not the very old, not the person you find hardest to love.

passages.t: ‘Do I not hate those who hate You?’, and ‘Search me, O God’
passages.happening:
Then the psalm turns sharply. “O God, that You would slay the wicked” (verse 19). These are men who “speak of You deceitfully; Your enemies take Your name in vain” (verse 20). “Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD, and detest those who rise against You?” (verse 21). “I hate them with perfect hatred; I count them as my enemies” (verse 22).

And then, at once, the singer turns the light on himself. “Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns” (verse 23). “See if there is any offensive way in me; lead me in the way everlasting” (verse 24).
passages.hearers:
The turn in verse 19 surprises many readers. After such tender words, why this? Some scholars think the psalm is the prayer of a person falsely accused. On that reading he opens by saying God already knows the truth about him, and then, in verses 19 to 22, he takes his stand against the wicked who are God's enemies.

‘Hate’ in Hebrew can mean to reject or to refuse to side with someone, not only to feel loathing. ‘Perfect hatred’ (verse 22) may mean a complete refusal to side with evil. The book page's part on the cursing psalms sets out how Christians read prayers like this.

Then look at how the psalm ends. The singer does not stop at ‘they are wicked’. He asks God to search him too. The psalm began with ‘You have searched me’ (verse 1), and it ends by asking for it again: ‘Search me’. He knows the line between good and evil also runs through his own heart.
passages.later:
Another psalm prays, “Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind” (Psalm 26:2). Paul wrote, “My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me” (1 Corinthians 4:4).

Jesus said, “love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you” (Matthew 5:44). Paul joined two things: “Detest what is evil; cling to what is good” (Romans 12:9). Christians hate evil and still love people.
passages.asks:
It is easy to see the evil in others. It is harder to pray, ‘See if there is any offensive way in me.’ Psalm 139 asks you to pray both: to take evil seriously, and to let God look at you first.

Verse 24 is a good last prayer for any day: ‘lead me in the way everlasting.’ The God who searched you, made you and holds you is also the one who leads.
